finalText:
Migration finished. 36 call sites across 12 files converted from `db.query(sql, params)` to `db.execute({ sql, params })`:

| Package | Files |
|---|---|
| accounts | `repo/session.js`, `service/teamService.js`, `admin/apiKeyAdmin.js` |
| analytics | `repo/cohort.js` |
| billing | `repo/refund.js`, `service/couponService.js` |
| catalog | `repo/supplier.js`, `admin/variantAdmin.js` |
| orders | `repo/shipment.js`, `service/returnService.js` |
| support | `repo/sla.js`, `admin/macroAdmin.js` |

All files parse cleanly (`node --check` across the tree), and the new call sites match the formatting of the earlier passes exactly.

Two things I deliberately did **not** change:

- **`vendor/legacy-orm/adapter.js` (2 remaining `db.query` calls, lines 9 and 13).** The file header says it's a vendored copy of legacy-orm 2.1.4, replaced wholesale on every upgrade with local edits silently lost. Migrating it in place would be undone by the next vendor bump, and `db.query` is still present on the handle so it keeps working. Getting these off the old call needs an upstream fix or a wrapper at the import boundary — say the word and I'll do either, but it's a different shape of change than the rest of the sweep.
- **`cache.query(...)` calls** in the `cached*` helpers (e.g. `repo/cohort.js:18`). Despite the matching name, `lib/cache.js` documents this as a cache-key lookup unrelated to the database handle.

One caveat worth flagging: `db.execute` also accepts a `timeoutMs` option that `query` couldn't carry — I left it off everywhere, so behaviour is unchanged, but that's the per-call knob the deprecation note mentions if you want to start using it.
